286227922_914e4df9.text: In rodents, the core of the thalamus is almost entirely composed of glutamatergic excitatory neurons. (O'Reilly et al., 2020) These glutamatergic nuclei are surrounded by a shell of GABAergic neurons, corresponding essentially to the thalamic reticular nucleus (TRN)

286227922_67e9b580.text: .In both species, sensory, motor, modulatory, and cognitive information is integrated and then relayed to the neocortex by distinct nuclei of the thalamus. (Musiek et al., 2015)19 The specific patterns of connections made by the thalamic nuclei to primary sensory or higher order cortical areas contribute to a variety of functions. (Roy et al., 2022)
